newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Oct 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Oct 3.

text.p: The following is a summary of major Indonesian political and business stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Jakarta. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (6221) 384-6364. Fax: (6221) 344-8404.

National logisitics agency BULOG has been ordered by President Suharto to implement market intervention operations to control the price of rice, wheat flour, cooking oil and sugar. The order came after figures were released showing that Indonesia had experienced a negative inflation rate of 0.04 percent in September.
A landslide on the special industrial island of Batam has killed at least 16 people and left four injured.

Japan and the United States have renewed complaints about Indonesia's contreversial national car policy which they say breaks World Trade Organisation (WTO) rules. The Timor sedan was released from customs earlier this week.

Indonesia's National Commission on Human Rights has said around 30 people are still missing following riots in the city in July. An earlier report in August by the commission put the total missing at 74.

The new head of Indonesia's National Commission on Human Rights said that the commission should be more independent. Munawir Sjadzali was elected chairman of the commission earlier this week to replace the late founding chairman Ali Said.

Forestry Minister Djamaludin Soeryohadikusumo has admited that 450 forest concessionaires have not lived up to their obligations to set aside five percent of their wood for domestic industries and they were being threatened with a warning.
Industry and Trade Minister Tunky Ariwibowo said Indonesia was ready to face any complaint made by Japan or the United States to the WTO over its controversial national car policy.
